page: Microsoft Azure M32bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, relying instead on external premium block storage.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong performance in specific single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. The instance achieves a strong rating in Geekbench single-core and multi-core tests, alongside high throughput in static web serving and gzip compression. Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 182.67 GB/sec for read operations and 86.71 GB/sec for writes. For machine learning workloads, the CPU's Advanced Matrix Extensions support average prompt processing speeds, but text generation performance drops to a weak 2.74 tokens/sec when running large 70B parameter models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the M32bs_v3 offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of local storage or GPU hardware. This makes it a balanced choice for enterprise databases, memory-intensive data processing, and software compilation. It is well-suited for workloads such as Redis caching, web serving, and medium-scale LLM inference, though it is not recommended for large-scale model text generation due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.
